theorems.statement: If A is a division algebra and a,b in A are nonzero, then ab is nonzero. Equivalently, an exact witness a!=0, b!=0, ab=0 certifies that A is not a division algebra.
For nonzero x in an eight-dimensional real positive-definite composition algebra, L_x/sqrt(N(x)) is in SO(8).
For finite r:X->S with fiber sizes m_s, sum_s (m_s)_k equals the number of ordered k-tuples of pairwise distinct elements of X having equal r-image.
theorems.novelty_status: bridge novelty unassessed; identity is elementary

theorems.statement: For nonzero real division octonions x,y, D(x,y)=U_x U_y U_xy^{-1} lies in SO(8), fixes the normalized xy direction, and equals I exactly when [x,y,z]=0 for every z.
theorems.novelty_status: bridge novelty unassessed; operator packaging may be new

theorems.statement: For a finite G-set X and G-invariant r:X->S, quotient occupancies are given fiberwise by Burnside averages and their falling-factorial sums count ordered distinct G-orbits with common r-image.
theorems.novelty_status: bridge novelty unassessed; arithmetic certificate application may be new

theorems.statement: For nonzero-norm x,y in an octonion composition algebra over F_q with q odd, Delta(x,y)=L_x L_y L_xy^{-1} belongs to O(C,N), fixes xy, and is identity exactly when [x,y,z]=0 for every z.
theorems.novelty_status: classical ingredients; finite defect-geometry packaging unassessed

theorems.statement: In any algebra, [a,b,c]d+[a,bc,d]+a[b,c,d]-[a,b,cd]-[ab,c,d]=0; equivalently, the signed associator defects around the five parenthesizations of a four-letter word form an exact closed boundary.
theorems.novelty_status: classical associator identity; finite boundary interpretation unassessed

theorems.statement: The committed eight-dimensional multiplication tensor over F3 passes the executable certificate for a unital alternative composition algebra and the recorded nonflat pentagon witness.
theorems.novelty_status: verified finite artifact; novelty not claimed

theorems.statement: For every n>6 over an odd finite field with char not dividing n, the split octonion norm admits a minimal (n-6)-dimensional discriminant-matching complement whose orthogonal sum is isometric to the n-dimensional Descartes curvature space; octonion defect operators extended by identity yield an embedding into its orthogonal group canonical up to conjugacy. For n=6 this holds exactly when -2/6 is a square.
theorems.novelty_status: classical Witt construction; defect-to-packing application unassessed
